utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon. By orders of the 18 March, 2003, from the President, I was designated pre-appeal judge for the present appeal. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-97-25-A, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krnojelac, can you hear the proceeding? THE APPELANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes I can hear the proceedings, and I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. THE APPELANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: May I then have the appearances, please. First, the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Christopher Staker. I appear with my colleague, Mr. Anthony Carmona. Our case manager today is Ms. Nicola Bonfield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the defendant, Mihajlo Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Pursuant to the Rule 65 bis, a Status Conference shall be held between 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The notices of appeal in this case were filed on 12th April, 2002, by the Defence, and on 15 April 2002 by the Prosecution. The last status conference was held on 26 November 2002. As you know, the purpose of the Status Conference is to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial and to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues to the custody of the person, including the mental and physical conditions of the person. I will ask now Mr. Krnojelac to express directly or through his counsel any concern in relation to the detention conditions. Then, we shall review the status of this appeal. Mr. Krnojelac, now, if you want, you can express directly or through your counsel about any concern in relation to the detention conditions. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. But I am in a situation in which it is very difficult for me to put it all in words. The course of the armed struggle onward, this whole period of time -- during this whole period of time, there was one problem following another. And all these problems have conduced to a serious impairment of my health. But also, the deaths which occurred during this time have contributed even more to the deterioration of my health. I'm sorry, but let me tell you that in 1965, one brother of mine died. In 1998, my sister died. And 60 days ago, another brother of mine died. And this Honourable Court showed that it was humane and allowed me, and I'd like to thank you for that, and I've also done so in writing to the Prosecutor's Office and the Chamber. I hope you have received it. Because I was allowed to get five days back home and see my own brother during the last hours of his life. My parents had nine children. Today, they have only me, and I have been here almost five years. Nonetheless, I have to be honest and say that regardless of this mood and my health, I nevertheless must thank Mrs. Vera [phoen] and especially the health personnel of the Detention Unit because they are doing all that they can to alleviate my problems, and thus somehow I manage to survive. But it is hard, and it is even harder when I have to say to Your Honour that I still consider myself innocent. However, I have been pronounced guilty, and therefore I hope that in the further proceedings, a number of things will be put right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood well, you have no specific complaint about the conditions, detention conditions? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I'm aware of one thing that I am where I am, that I have been there for a very long time, and the most important thing, since you're asking me, the most important thing about it all is I have absolutely no objections about the conduct of the personnel around me, they are treating me correctly. And I am also trying to behave like all normal people regardless of all these problems that I have just mentioned to you, because I must be aware of where I am even though I am Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 34 to 35. completely innocent. But there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: This brings us to the end of our discussion on the conditions of the Detention Unit now. And now we will start to deal with the status of the appeal. The filing in this appeal are complete. At the last Status Conference, there was the issue of the Rule 68 search and disclosure process undertaken by the Prosecution. Since then, the process has been completed by the Prosecution as shown in its fourth status report on disclosure. On 31st March, 2003, the appellant Krnojelac notified the Appeals Chamber that he would not file any additional evidence in these proceedings. Let me ask the Prosecution, therefore, the following question: While the appellant, Krnojelac, has no additional evidence to present, whether you would like to present any such evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not intend to file any motion under Rule 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. If both parties will not present any additional evidence, I would like to hear from you as to possible date and to facilitate the task of the Tribunal, starting from 1st of June, which will be convenient for the hearing on the merits of this appeal. Your answer will assist the Appeals Chamber to find a suitable date for both the parties and the Chamber. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution could be at the Appeals Chamber's disposal through the month of June. Yes, no particular date would be expressed. I don't know if Your Honour is seeking indications of appropriate times after June, but certainly from the 1st of June throughout that month, the Prosecution would not express a preference for any particular date but would defer to the convenience of the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, of course like the Prosecutor, I shall be ready as of the 1st of June, whatever date you fix, of course, I'm quite ready to accept it and go by it. But I'd like to ask nevertheless, and I repeat once again with all due respect, in view of the time we've spent waiting for the judgement of the first instance and in view of the health of the accused, could you perhaps consider the possibility if that could be done in May, that is, as early as possible, before June. And as for June, whenever you decide, the Defence will be ready to appear before the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, of course I will bear in mind your suggestion. And the Appeals Chamber in due course will announce the schedule for hearing on the substance of the appeal. And the schedule for hearing, taking into account the other scheduling matters, will be determined, as I said, bearing in mind your suggestion, but probably starting or after the beginning of June. Do the parties have any comment or question on these or any other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only other question may be the length of time that may be required for the hearings. Our estimate would be perhaps two to three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Okay. You can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: The only other question is how much time may be required for the hearing itself. Our estimate would be if it was set down for three days, that would be sufficient. It maybe take even less time than that. But that's simply our observation at this stage as it may assist the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You mean three days a week, if I've understood you well, you want to say if we start to work three days per week. Is that the idea?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I was talking about the length of time required in totality for the oral hearing in this appeal. And our estimate was that if the appeal was set down for three days of hearings, that that should be sufficient, and that it may be completed in less time than that. This was simply an estimate we give at this stage for the assistance of the Appeals Chamber in determining the scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the Defence wish to say something in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't quite understand my learned colleague. Is that the time that the Prosecution needs or did my learned friend also include the time for the Defence? If he thinks that that is the period of time which would suffice both for the Prosecution and Defence, yes, I do think it would suffice all together, the Prosecution and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Prosecutor, perhaps you should repeat what you have just said, just so that there is no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe there is accord between us and the Defence. The time frame that I estimated was the total time for the entire hearing for the Prosecution appeal and the Defence appeal and all submissions by both parties in both appeals. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I must say something. I hope that the Prosecutor's Office will not take up two and a half days and leave the Defence only half a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for these suggestions and countersuggestions. They will be taken into account. Thank you. [In English] Any other comments or any other issues? No. Okay. I understand that there are no further issues or questions to be dealt with at this Status Conference. And therefore, this Status Conference may now be adjourned.
